January 1910. Mahler, with his heart condition, travels between New York and Vienna and works on at his Tenth Symphony. In history he dies on 18 May 1911, leaving it unfinished.

January 1910.
You are Mahler. Three years ago you were told of your heart condition.
A great contract with the New York Philharmonic, the premiere of the 'Symphony of a Thousand', and the Tenth Symphony half written.
In history you die on 18 May 1911.

Cut down your work, see an eminent doctor, and finish the Tenth with your own hand.

1791: save Mozart
Mozart is not made to rest. He will not put down his pen.
Can you change history? Eighteen months to the night of fate.
Debts, overwork, the grey messenger. Commissions bring money but eat away the body. Call an eminent doctor, choose the commissions, and bring Mozart past 5 December.

Vienna, June 1790.
Mozart is 34. His debts are mounting and work from the court is scarce.
In history he dies on 5 December 1791.

The commissions that arrive from now on bring money and fame but eat away his body. Call an eminent doctor, choose which commissions to accept, and bring him through the night of fate.
Mozart himself will not rest.
The coronation at Frankfurt
The court orchestra was not summoned to the coronation of the new Emperor Leopold II. Mozart means to go to Frankfurt at his own expense, even if he has to pawn the silver.
Let him go<small>-400 fr, fame +15, a strain on the body (chance ↓)</small>
Mozart went to Frankfurt at his own expense. The concert was praised but made almost nothing.
Stay in Vienna<small>rest the body (chance ↑)</small>
Mozart stayed in Vienna and devoted himself to composing.
A farewell evening with Haydn
Haydn is leaving for London. At the farewell dinner Mozart murmured: 'I feel we shall never meet again.'
Talk until morning<small>chance ↑ (support for the heart)</small>
Mozart and Haydn talked late into the night.
Send him to bed early<small>chance ↑ (a little)</small>
Schikaneder's commission
His old friend the impresario Schikaneder has come to ask for a popular German opera for his suburban theatre. The title: Die Zauberflöte. He wants it by the summer.
Accept<small>a great hit in the autumn (+1,200 fr, fame +30). But overwork (chance ↓)</small>
Mozart accepted Die Zauberflöte.

The grey messenger

A man in grey who gave no name came to commission a Requiem. He left half the fee in advance.
The patron is said to have been a count who meant to pass the work off as his own, in memory of his late wife.
Accept<small>+450 fr. He is haunted by the shadow of death (chance ↓). If he overcomes fate he can finish the Requiem himself</small>
Mozart accepted the Requiem from an anonymous patron. To his wife he let slip: 'I feel I am writing a Requiem for myself.'
The grey messenger left without a word.
An urgent commission from Prague
An opera for the Emperor's coronation, La clemenza di Tito, to be written in barely three weeks — with the long journey to Prague besides.
Accept<small>+900 fr, fame +20. He falls ill on the journey (chance ↓↓)</small>
Mozart went on writing even in the coach and finished La clemenza di Tito.

Mozart lived
5 December 1791
Day broke. Mozart got up and, before anything else, began writing the rest of the Requiem. From here the history of music takes another road.
Everything was done, but history did not change. The unfinished Requiem was left on the desk.
Rival divas

In London in 1727 the partisans of the two divas caused an uproar in the house, and the performance was broken off. The story that they 'came to blows on stage' is thought to be a fabrication spread by the satires of the day.
Sworn rivals
London's opera house split into a Handel party and a Bononcini party.
Constant clashes
The great castrato Senesino clashed with Handel again and again.
A duel in the past
In 1704 the young Handel and Mattheson quarrelled and fought a duel with swords. A button stopped the blade and a life was spared.
A deep friendship
Haydn called Mozart 'the greatest composer', and Mozart dedicated six string quartets to Haydn.
An awkward master and pupil
Beethoven studied with Haydn but is said to have grumbled that he 'learned nothing' from him.
Husband and wife
Robert and Clara married in the teeth of fierce opposition from Clara's father.
Friendship (that cooled in time)
As young men the two were close in Paris, but later a distance grew between them.
In 1837 the 'piano duel' between Liszt and Thalberg took place in Paris.
Allies
Liszt arranged Berlioz's Symphonie fantastique for piano and made it widely known.
Devotion
Brahms revered Clara Schumann all his life.
Close friends
Brahms and Joachim were close friends from their youth. The Violin Concerto was written for Joachim.
Supporter
The conductor Bülow made famous the phrase 'the three Bs': Bach, Beethoven, Brahms.
A tangled history
Bülow supported Wagner by conducting the premieres of his music dramas, but his wife Cosima later became Wagner's.
Cold war of the schools
Around the two men the musical world split into the 'New German School' and the 'conservatives'.
Clash and reconciliation
Rubinstein savaged Tchaikovsky's First Piano Concerto as 'unplayable'. Later they were reconciled and he played it.
Bruno Walter learned as Mahler's assistant and later gave the premiere of Das Lied von der Erde.
Worthy rivals
The two performed each other's works, but in character they were complete opposites.
Debussy and Satie talked for years in the cafés of Paris.
Stravinsky studied composition with Rimsky-Korsakov.
